patch_description:
This ansatz uses a parameter-efficient butterfly topology rather than the seed’s nearest-neighbor CZ line. Independent RY rotations first select a measurement basis for each qubit, while four shared RZ parameters provide regularized phase corrections across paired wires. Two complementary CNOT matchings then propagate pairwise phase information globally in only two entangling stages. Parametrized CRY gates between the stages add controlled, noncommuting mixing, and a final independent RY layer converts the resulting phase correlations into the Z populations used by the fixed readout.

The design uses 20 trainable parameters per block: enough local freedom to distinguish feature-pair roles, but substantially constrained phase and controlled-mixing parameters to reduce overfitting. The alternating long-range matchings also align naturally with the complete set of 28 two-qubit feature couplings without reproducing the seed’s linear-entanglement approach.
